Read History Go to My Account Log Out News Africa’s next growth chapter in focus as Vera Songwe, others lead discussion at Gahawards summit Vera Songwe, UN former under-Secretary will, among other experts, lead discussion on “The New Africa Economy: Vision, Capital & Influence’
Listen to this article Share Vera Songwe, UN former under-Secretary will, among other experts, lead discussion on “The New Africa Economy: Vision, Capital & Influence’ when business leaders converge on Lagos for Gahawards and business summit mid December, 2026. “This year’s agenda puts the financing of African growth at the centre of the discussion. How can African businesses secure the long-term capital they need to expand production, reach customers across borders and create jobs?” The organisers further said that the programme will examine the role of investors, policymakers and business leaders in financing enterprise and infrastructure, reducing barriers to regional trade and strengthening Africa’s voice in global investment decisions. These discussions draw on the ambitions of the African Continental Free Trade Area and African Union Agenda 2063. According to the organisers, other speakers expected at the summit include Lere Baale, Director at Business School Netherlands Nigeria; Oluwatoyin F. Sanni, investment banker and Group CEO of Emerging Africa Group; and Adebola Williams, Co-Founder and CEO of RED and a political strategist and nation-branding expert. Others are Chris Ogbechie, Professor of Strategic Management at Lagos Business School; and Ahmadou Aly Mbaye Professor of Economics and Public Policy at Cheikh Anta Diop University in Dakar while UAE Consul General Salem Aljaberi will join as special guest, according to the statement from the organisers. The summit which is expected to draw approximately 1,200 delegates from finance, diplomacy, government, industry and academia will combine more keynote addresses, policy and business panels, executive networking and the GAH Awards. The statement said leadership and diplomatic Representation, Princess Oghene, Founder and Executive Chair of the GAH Awards & Business Summit and Founder & Group CEO of GMYT Group Ltd., will convene this 14th edition. .“A business owner deciding whether to open a second factory needs to know whether he or she can finance it, whether business owner can reach customers across borders and whether the rules will hold long enough for the owner to invest,” said Princess Oghene in the statement. “Those are decisions that investors, governments and entrepreneurs often discuss in separate rooms. We are bringing them together in Lagos to examine what each can do to make the next investment possible”, she said. Describing Vera as a perfect individual to lead discussion on the subject, the organisers said her work on African capital markets and development finance speaks directly to one of the summit’s central concerns, the cost of financing growth. The statement said the 13th edition, “Africa Reimagined: Innovation, Inclusion & Sustainable Growth,” drew more than 1,000 guests in December last year.
